The '''2022–23 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The season marked the program's 107th season and its 106th consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Wolverines were led by fourth-year head coach [[Juwan Howard]], and played their home games for the 56th consecutive year at [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].

==Regular season==
===November===
Michigan began the season on November 7 with a 75–56 victory over [[2022–23 Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball team|Purdue Fort Wayne]]. Michigan was led by [[Hunter Dickinson]] with a game-high 22 points and 12 rebounds, for his 18th career double-double, while [[Jett Howard]] added 21 points. Dickinson reached 1,000 career points on a free throw with 3:43 remaining in the first half, becoming the 57th Wolverine to reach the milestone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/7/mens-basketball-dickinson-captures-1000th-career-point-as-u-m-defeats-purdue-fort-wayne-in-season-opener.aspx|title=Dickinson Captures 1000th Career Point as U-M Defeats Purdue Fort Wayne in Season Opener|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=November 7, 2022|date=November 7, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 11, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball team|Eastern Michigan]] 88–83. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 31 points, while Terrance Williams II added 18 points and a career-high 11 rebounds for his first career double-double. Dickinson tied a career-high with 13 field goals made on 17 attempts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401483366|title=Emoni Bates scores career-high 30 in EMU's loss to No. 22 UM|date=November 11, 2022|access-date=November 12, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/11/mens-basketball-michigan-rallies-past-eastern-michigan-behind-31-points-from-dickinson.aspx|title=Michigan Rallies Past Eastern Michigan Behind 31 Points from Dickinson|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 11, 2022|access-date=November 12, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 14, Dickinson and Howard were named the Big Ten Player of the Week and Big Ten Freshman of the Week, respectively. Dickinson averaged 26.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 1.5 blocked shots, while Howard averaged 15.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals, and 1.5 blocked shots in Michigan's two victories last week.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/14/2022-23-michigan-mens-basketball-awards-and-honors.aspx|title=Awards and Honors: Dickinson, Howard Sweep Big Ten Weekly Honors|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 14, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/11/14/general-michigan-sweeps-weekly-mens-basketball-accolades.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114194701/https://bigten.org/news/2022/11/14/general-michigan-sweeps-weekly-mens-basketball-accolades.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 14, 2022|title=Michigan Sweeps Weekly Men's Basketball Accolades|date=November 14, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]|website=BigTen.org}}</ref> On November 16, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] 91–60 in the semifinals of the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]]. Michigan was led by Howard with a game-high 17 points, while [[Kobe Bufkin]] and [[Joey Baker]] added 14 points each, and Dickinson added 11 points and seven rebounds. With seven rebounds, Dickinson became the 46th Wolverine to reach the 500 rebounds milestone. After reaching 1,000 points in the season-opener against Purdue Fort Wayne, he became the 31st member of Michigan's 1000 point/500 rebound club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/16/mens-basketball-howard-bufkin-lead-michigan-rout-of-pittsburgh-in-legends-classic-opener.aspx|title=Howard, Bufkin Lead Michigan Rout of Pittsburgh in Legends Classic Opener|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> The next day Michigan lost to [[2022–23 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] 87–62 in the Legends Classic championship game. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 14 points, while Howard added 12 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/18/mens-basketball-michigan-falls-to-arizona-state-in-legends-classic-final.aspx|title=Michigan Falls to Arizona State in Legends Classic Final|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 18, 2022|access-date=November 18, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 20, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]] 70–66 in overtime. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 24 points and 14 rebounds for his 19th career double-double, while Howard added 14 points and a career-high four blocks, and Jaelin Llewellyn added 10 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/20/mens-basketball-michigan-kicks-off-homestand-with-overtime-victory-defeats-ohio-70-66.aspx|title=Michigan Kicks Off Homestand with Overtime Victory, Defeats Ohio 70-66|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 20, 2022|access-date=November 20, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 23, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Jackson State Tigers basketball team|Jackson State]] 78–68. Michigan was led by Howard with a game-high 19 points, while Williams added 11 points, Bufkin added 10 points and a career-high three blocks, and Dickinson added nine points and 12 rebounds, one-point shy of a double-double. Michigan's defense blocked 13 shots, tied for the second-most in a single game in program history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/23/mens-basketball-howard-williams-ii-lead-u-m-to-victory-over-visiting-jackson-state.aspx|title=Howard, Williams II Lead U-M to Victory Over Visiting Jackson State|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 23, 2022|access-date=November 23, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 29, Michigan lost to (No. 3 [[AP Poll]]/No. 3 [[Coaches Poll]]) [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] 70–68 in the [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]]. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 23 points, while Howard added 15 points and Bufkin added 11 points. This was Howard's fifth consecutive game scoring in double figures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/11/30/mens-basketball-upset-bid-comes-up-short-as-michigan-falls-to-third-ranked-virginia-70-68.aspx|title=Upset Bid Comes up Short as Michigan Falls to Third-Ranked Virginia, 70-68|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 30, 2022|access-date=November 30, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===December===
On December 4, Michigan lost to (No. 19 AP Poll/No. 18 Coaches Poll) [[2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] 73–69 in the Basketball Hall of Fame London Showcase. ===January===
On January 1, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] 81–46. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a season-high 32 points and 12 rebounds for his 20th career double-double, while Williams II added 11 points. Michigan's defense held Maryland to just 13 first-half points, which tied the program record for fewest first-half points allowed. The Wolverines's opened the game on a 17–0 scoring run, including shooting 7-for-7 from the field.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/1/1/mens-basketball-happy-new-year-michigan-rebounds-with-rout-of-maryland-to-begin-2023.aspx|title=Happy New Year: Michigan Rebounds With Rout of Maryland to Begin 2023|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=January 1, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On January 4, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]] 79–69. ===February===
On February 2, Michigan defeated Northwestern 68–51. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 19 points, while Bufkin added 15 points, a career-high 12 rebounds and eight assists, for his first career double-double, Baker added a season high 14 points, and McDaniel added a career-high nine assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/2/mens-basketball-bufkin-notches-first-career-double-double-in-win-at-northwestern.aspx|title=Bufkin Notches First Career Double-Double in Win at Northwestern|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 2, 2023|access-date=February 2, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 5, Michigan won their [[Michigan–Ohio State men's basketball rivalry|rivalry]] game against [[2022–23 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] 77–69. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 26 points and 11 rebounds, for his 24th career double-double, while Howard added 16 points and Bufkin added 13 points, eight rebounds and five assists. With his double-double Dickinson tied [[Glen Rice]] for 12th most all-time in Michigan program history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/5/mens-basketball-strong-performance-by-dickinson-leads-u-m-over-rival-osu.aspx|title=Strong Performance by Dickinson Leads U-M over Rival OSU|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 5, 2023|access-date=February 5, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 8, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 93–72. Michigan was led by Howard with 22 points, while Dickinson added 16 points and 10 rebounds, for his 25th career double-double, McDaniel added 14 points and four assists, Bufkin added 13 points, seven rebounds and five assists, Baker added 11 points, and Williams II added 10 points and five rebounds. This marked the first time six Wolverines scored in double figures since December 6, 2019. With his double-double, Dickinson tied [[C. J. Kupec]] for 11th most all-time in Michigan program history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/8/mens-basketball-high-octane-offense-fuels-michigan-win-over-nebraska.aspx|title=High-Octane Offense Fuels Michigan Win Over Nebraska|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 8, 2023|access-date=February 8, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 11, Michigan lost to (No. 18 AP Poll/No. 18 Coaches Poll) [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] 62–61. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 16 points, seven rebounds and three blocks, while Bufkin added 14 points, Howard added 12 points, and Tarris Reed Jr. added a career-high eight points and five rebounds. With three blocks, Dickinson became the third Wolverine to record 40 blocks in three consecutive seasons. Michigan was held scoreless during the final five minutes of the game, while neither team scored in the final three minutes of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/11/mens-basketball-late-scoring-pushes-hoosiers-past-wolverines.aspx|title=Late Scoring Pushes Hoosiers Past Wolverines|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 11, 2023|access-date=February 11, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 14, Michigan lost to [[2022–23 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] 64–59. Michigan was led by Bufkin with 21 points, while Dickinson added 12 points and 12 rebounds, for his 26th career double-double. With his double-double, Dickinson tied [[Campy Russell]] for 10th most all-time in Michigan program history. [[Will Tschetter]] started his first career game, playing 26 minutes while recording four points and five rebounds. He replaced Williams II, who missed the game with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/15/mens-basketball-late-game-defense-not-enough-as-michigan-falls-at-wisconsin.aspx|title=Late Game Defense Not Enough as Michigan Falls at Wisconsin|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 18, Michigan won their rivalry game against Michigan State 84–72, in Michigan State's first game since the [[2023 Michigan State University shooting|Michigan State University shooting]]. Michigan was led by McDaniel with a career-high 18 points, while Bufkin added 17 points, Dickinson added 10 points and seven rebounds, Howard added 10 points, Baker added 10 points and Reed added eight points and a career-high 10 rebounds. Michigan ended the game on a 12–0 run, holding Michigan State scoreless for the final 2:29 of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/18/mens-basketball-emotional-evening-sees-michigan-rally-for-maize-out-victory-over-michigan-state.aspx|title=Emotional Evening Sees Michigan Rally for Maize Out Victory over Michigan State|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 18, 2023|access-date=February 18, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 23, Michigan defeated [[2022–23 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] 58–45. Michigan was led by McDaniel with a game-high 16 points, and career-high five steals, while Bufkin added 14 points, and Dickinson added 13 points and 11 rebounds, for his 27th career double-double. McDaniel's five steals were the most for a Wolverine since [[Zavier Simpson]] also had five steals in a game against [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] on November 14, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/23/mens-basketball-michigan-defense-shines-in-gritty-road-win-over-rutgers.aspx|title=Michigan Defense Shines in Gritty Road Win Over Rutgers|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 23, 2023|access-date=February 23, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On February 26, Michigan defeated Wisconsin 87–79 in overtime. Michigan outscored Wisconsin 19–11 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/2/26/mens-basketball-dickinsons-buzzer-beater-forces-ot-in-u-m-win-over-wisconsin.aspx|title=Dickinson's Buzzer-Beater Forces OT in U-M Win Over Wisconsin|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=February 26, 2023|access-date=February 26, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===March===
On March 2, Michigan lost to [[2022–23 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] 91–87 in double-overtime. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 31 points, and a career-high 16 rebounds, for his 29th double-double, while Bufkin added 23 points, and Howard added 15 points. This marked Michigan's first double-overtime game since [[2019–20 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2020]]. With a three-pointer in the first quarter, Dickinson became the 22nd Wolverine to reach the 1,500 point milestone. With his 31 points, Dickinson surpassed current head coach Juwan Howard (1,526) for 20th on Michigan's all-time scoring list.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/2/mens-basketball-michigan-drops-double-overtime-heartbreaker-at-illinois.aspx|title=Michigan Drops Double-Overtime Heartbreaker at Illinois|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On March 5, Michigan lost to (No. 15 AP Poll/No. 13 Coaches Poll) Indiana 75–73 in overtime. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 24 points, 14 rebounds, and a career-high tying five blocks, for his 30th career double-double, while Bufkin added 19 points, Howard added 16 points and McDaniel added 10 points. With 14 rebounds, Dickinson became the ninth Wolverine to surpass the 750-rebound mark, and the sixth Wolverine to reach 1,500 points and 750 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/5/mens-basketball-michigan-drops-overtime-battle-at-no-15-indiana.aspx|title=Michigan Drops Overtime Battle at No. 15 Indiana|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 5, 2023|access-date=March 5, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

==Postseason==
===Big Ten tournament===
On March 9, Michigan opened its [[2023 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] play with a 62–50 loss to Rutgers in the second round. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 24 points, seven rebounds and three blocks, while Bufkin added nine points, seven rebounds and five assists. Michigan struggled in the second half, scoring only one field goal until the final minute of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/9/mens-basketball-michigan-falls-to-rutgers-in-big-ten-tournament-after-second-half-struggles.aspx|title=Michigan Falls to Rutgers In Big Ten Tournament After Second-Half Struggles|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 9, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401514416|title=Rutgers pulls away in 2nd half vs. frigid-shooting Michigan|date=March 9, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

===NIT tournament===
On March 12, Michigan received and accepted an at-large bid to the [[2023 National Invitation Tournament]] as the No. 3 seed. This was the Wolverines' first [[National Invitation Tournament]] appearance since [[2007 National Invitation Tournament|2007]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/12/mens-basketball-wolverines-set-to-host-toledo-in-opening-round-of-nit.aspx|title=Wolverines Set to Host Toledo in Opening Round of NIT|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 12, 2023|access-date=March 12, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On March 14, Michigan began their participation in the 2023 NIT with a 90–80 victory over [[2022–23 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]] in the first round. Michigan was led by Bufkin with a game-high 23 points, eight rebounds and five assists, while Baker added a season-high 21 points, Dickinson added 19 points and nine rebounds, one rebound shy of a double-double, and McDaniel added 16 points and eight assists. Michigan shot a season-high 57 percent (13-for-23) from three-point range.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/14/mens-basketball-sharp-shooting-propels-michigan-to-win-over-toledo-in-nit-first-round.aspx|title=Sharp Shooting Propels Michigan to Win over Toledo in NIT First Round|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 14, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

On March 18, Michigan lost to [[2022–23 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] in the second round. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 21 points and 11 rebounds, for his 31st career double-double, while McDaniel added 19 points, five rebounds, and three assists, and Baker added 11 points. Michigan opened the game with a 5–0 lead, before Vanderbilt answered with a 17–0 run to force a Michigan timeout with 12:51. Michigan responded with a 15–3 run to tie the game at 20. During the final five minutes of the half the teams shot a combined 33 percent (five-for-15) from the field, and Michigan led the game 30–29 at half-time. Vanderbilt took advantage of three Michigan turnovers in the final minute of the game to go on a 9–0 run and take a one-point lead with 12 seconds remaining in the game. Michigan missed layup attempts by McDaniel and Dickinson in the final seconds, and Vanderbilt won the game. Youssef Khayat started in his first career game, replacing an injured Bufkin, and scored three points and three rebounds in 17 minutes. With his double-double Dickinson tied [[Loy Vaught]] for sixth most all-time in Michigan program history. McDaniel became the sixth Michigan freshman to record at least 250 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists in their freshman season, and the first since [[Derrick Walton Jr.]] in [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/3/18/mens-basketball-late-vanderbilt-surge-ends-michigans-nit-run-season.aspx|title=Late Vanderbilt Surge Ends Michigan's NIT Run, Season|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=March 18, 2023|access-date=March 18, 2023|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>
